questions.q: How does Finance's request genuinely differ from the Executive's or the Board's, rather than just being "the same dashboard in Excel"?
options: Finance wants a workbook they can manipulate themselves with their own formulas, not a dashboard they only view
Finance's request is identical to the Board's in every respect
Finance doesn't need any real numbers, only estimates
Finance wants a tool that auto-refreshes faster than Power BI
questions.explain: Finance's job-to-be-done is auditing and re-summing numbers themselves, which is a genuinely different requirement from viewing a dashboard.

questions.q: How does the CSV export built for Finance differ from the star-schema model Power BI and Tableau use?
options: It contains the same surrogate keys and separate tables, just saved as a CSV
It flattens the fact table and three dimensions into one human-readable table with real column names and real dates, exposing no surrogate keys
It only contains ProductKey and TerritoryKey, with no measures at all
It is identical to the raw Sales.SalesOrderDetail table with no joins applied
questions.explain: The export collapses the warehouse's separate dimension tables and surrogate keys into one flat sheet with real, readable values — a format suited to how a spreadsheet actually works.

questions.q: Why does Finance's workbook deliberately use a static, point-in-time export instead of a live connection to the warehouse?
options: Excel is technically incapable of connecting to SQL Server at all
Finance's job is to sign off on a specific, frozen set of numbers for one specific quarter — a constantly-changing live connection would work against that goal
Static exports are always more accurate than live connections
The warehouse blocks all connections from Excel specifically
questions.explain: A live, auto-refreshing connection would undermine Finance's actual need to sign off on a fixed, specific set of numbers at one point in time.

questions.q: Which real warehouse tables does the export query join together to build Finance's flat extract?
options: Only dw.FactProductSales, with no joins at all
dw.FactProductSales joined to dw.DimDate, dw.DimProduct, and dw.DimTerritory
dw.DimSalesReason and dw.BridgeOrderSalesReason only
Sales.SalesOrderDetail and Sales.SalesOrderHeader directly, bypassing the warehouse
questions.explain: The export joins the fact table to DimDate (for a real date), DimProduct, and DimTerritory, flattening them into one row per order line with readable columns.

questions.q: Why might it be a mistake to treat Finance's Excel workbook as the least technically interesting of the three deliverables?
options: Because it actually uses more advanced DAX than Power BI
Because its independence from the other two tools is exactly what later lets it genuinely catch a real mistake the other two deliverables don't reveal
Because Excel workbooks are always more complex than Tableau dashboards
Because Finance's workbook will replace the warehouse entirely
questions.explain: Being built completely independently is precisely what makes Finance's workbook capable of surfacing a discrepancy — which becomes the center of Chapter 7.
